clue.text: Spiritualist meeting held by wise ancestors …

indicators.note: the answer is held by the words wise ancestors, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A gathering of mediums is hosted by sage forebears, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 4 across in surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering where people try to contact the dead is the classic spiritualist sitting.

clue.text: Ill-feeling if rest gets disturbed

indicators.note: gets disturbed means the letters of if rest are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grows bad-tempered when their sleep is interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is conflict or discord, the hostility of a bitter quarrel.

clue.text: Slur like individual swallowing last of Asti

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the individual word contains the next piece

parts.note: a person is an individual

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the word Asti

explanation.surface: Someone's speech slurs after gulping down the sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine; 'Slur' fits slurred drinking but means an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging remark, a smear on someone's reputation.

clue.text: Apple company's almost sluggish

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, and the apostrophe s adds S

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the sluggish word loses its last letter

parts.note: tardy means slow, sluggish

explanation.surface: A fruit firm is described as nearly slothful.
explanation.definitionFit: Costard is an old English variety of cooking apple, large and ribbed.

clue.text: … sanctified and authorised by Church finally

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Church

parts.note: authorised means allowed, permitted

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1 across: the meeting is blessed and finally sanctioned by the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made holy or consecrated is hallowed, as in hallowed ground.

clue.text: Aid by encouraging transgression initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the four preceding words

explanation.surface: Helping someone by urging them to do wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage someone in wrongdoing, as in aiding and abetting.

clue.text: Dirges using feeble notes, oddly

parts.note: a lame excuse is a feeble one

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word notes, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Funeral songs played with weak, strange notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Laments are songs of mourning, as dirges are.

clue.text: Draw in chain holding hoist

indicators.note: holding means the words draw in chain contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Pulling a chain in to lift something heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch is a crank-driven device for lifting loads, a type of lifting gear.

clue.text: Delicate record — Queen support rises

parts.note: a disc is a record
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: rises in a down clue means the word for support is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A fragile vinyl disc, with royal backing climbing in value.
explanation.definitionFit: Discreet means tactful and careful, as delicate handling of a matter is.

clue.text: Increased taking exercise, tossing in sleep

indicators.note: tossing suggests things thrown about, so the combined letters are jumbled

parts.note: increased means rose, went up
PE is physical exercise, physical education

explanation.surface: Someone working out more and more, then tossing and turning in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' just joins the two pieces before 'tossing' mixes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is rest or slumber, a synonym for sleep.

clue.text: Time runs out to get final goal

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of time runs are put out of order

explanation.surface: As the clock runs down, a team scores the decisive last goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final goal' looks like football; it is the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the last stop or end point, so an ultimate destination.

clue.text: See this person in total heaven

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see

indicators.note: in puts the self-reference inside the word for total

parts.note: a sum is a total
this person is the setter speaking of themself, I

explanation.surface: Seeing oneself completely in paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb; it is a bishop's diocese. Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysium is the paradise of Greek myth, a state of perfect bliss.

clue.text: Properly in favour of male friend

parts.note: in favour of means for, supporting
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone rightly backs a male companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something formally means doing it in the correct, official manner.

clue.text: A new task detailed for newsreader

indicators.note: detailed read as de-tailed means the word loses its tail letter

parts.note: a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: A fresh assignment is spelled out for a television presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'set out in detail' but means de-tailed: CHORE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor, short for anchorman or anchorwoman, presents a news broadcast.

clue.text: Dressed down in price, wearing sack

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the price word is covered by the sack word

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed
a rate is a price, as in rate for the job

explanation.surface: Clothes reduced in price, as if wearing a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed down here means told off, scolded, as berated does.

clue.text: Key spies blend in somehow, casing area

indicators.note: casing means wrapping round, so the jumbled letters enclose the next piece
somehow says the letters of spies blend in are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Undercover agents merge into the crowd while scoping out a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casing' plays on criminals casing a joint; here the anagram of SPIES BLEND IN surrounds A.
explanation.definitionFit: Key as an adjective means crucial or essential, which is what indispensable means.

clue.text: Strapping body maturing

parts.note: a band is a body of people
aging means maturing, growing older

explanation.surface: A muscular physique growing more developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strapping' looks like burly; it means wrapping in strips.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapping is the act of binding a wound or joint, like wrapping a dressing.

clue.text: One unwilling to strike poet that holds dagger

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A pacifist poet carries a concealed knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a blow, fitting a dagger; it is industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is a sheath that holds a blade such as a sword or knife.

clue.text: Arrangement for auctioning rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb or adjective means poor or disordered, signalling the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lot of junk is laid out for sale at auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A configuration is the layout or arrangement of parts.

clue.text: Animal's pong accepted by one elderly relative

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so the elderly relative contains the smell word

parts.note: nan is British for grandmother
hum and pong are both British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Granny puts up with the stink of a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' looks like a noun, but here it is the adjective, brutish.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means brutish, lacking compassion, which is what inhuman means.

clue.text: Love that is about solid, sort of?

indicators.note: about means around, so the abbreviation surrounds the anagrammed letters

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: sort of means sorted, rearranged, so the word solid is shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone muses on whether love is a solid kind of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the verb here, and 'sort of' is the anagram signal for solid, not a hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to adore them, worshipping them as a hero.

clue.text: Book's bound to be gripped in both hands

indicators.note: gripped in means held between, so the bound word sits inside the hands

parts.note: both hands are left and right, L and R
a bound is a boundary or edge

explanation.surface: A bound book is held in both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' suggests bookbinding, but it is a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger is an account book in which financial records are kept.

clue.text: Throw goes over pitch, getting obstreperous

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for pitch is read backwards

parts.note: to pitch or lob is to throw in a high arc
a shy is a throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A cricket delivery flies past the wicket and tempers flare.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshy is British slang for rebellious and awkward, from Bolshevik, close to unruly.

clue.text: Carry empty 'Equalizer' gun

parts.note: to lug is to carry something heavy

indicators.note: empty means removing the inside of the word Equalizer, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Lugging around a pistol called the Equalizer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equalizer' is old American slang for a gun, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol.

clue.text: Rendezvous, embracing miss turning bare

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the date wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting, a rendezvous

indicators.note: turning means the word for miss is read the other way round

parts.note: to miss something is to lose it

explanation.surface: A lovers' meeting where a young woman is hugged turns stark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a young woman but is the verb, to lose; 'turning' reverses it to ESOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A desolate landscape is bleak and empty, so bare.

clue.text: See stake mount up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the mountain name reads from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Etna is a volcanic mountain in Sicily

explanation.surface: Watch the bets climb higher.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake each poker player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: Case with a hole plugged by adhesive

indicators.note: plugged by means filled with, so the hole word has the adhesive put inside it

parts.note: a rent is a tear or hole in fabric
gum is an adhesive, glue

explanation.surface: A container with a puncture is patched up with glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a box; it is a case made in debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal or logical case is a line of reasoning put forward to persuade.

clue.text: Group penning single's making progress

indicators.note: penning means shutting in, as in a pen, so the group word encloses the next piece

parts.note: a ring is a group or gang, as in a spy ring
single is I, the Roman one, and the apostrophe s supplies S

explanation.surface: A band writes a hit single that climbs the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like songwriting; it means enclosing, as in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising means going up or advancing, as a rising star is getting on.

clue.text: Distracted being buzzed during performance

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the buzzed word sits inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
to buzz someone is to ring them, so buzzed means rang

explanation.surface: An actor is put off when a phone buzzes mid-show.
explanation.definitionFit: Distracted in the old sense of driven mad, which is what deranged means.

clue.text: Scrounger that's sometimes pickled in pub

indicators.note: in places the egg inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
pickled eggs are a traditional British pub snack, so an egg is something sometimes pickled

explanation.surface: A cadger is often found drunk in the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' suggests drunk; it is literal. Pickled eggs are a traditional jarred snack on British pub counters.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar asks others for money or food, as a scrounger does.
